changelog: Fixed a second trigger for the v3.26.0 chart-stretching bug: a double-click on the Backtesting replay chart no longer calls fitContent() (the library's own 'cram everything into view' reset) during an active session -- it now does what the Jump to Latest button does: restore the session's own fixed bar spacing, resume auto-follow, and scroll to the live edge. Found via real-browser Playwright verification of v3.26.0, not part of that release's own audit (it isn't in the Play/Next Bar/Rewind step path).

Audited every other reachable caller of fitContent()/setVisibleLogicalRange()/setVisibleRange() in js/chart.js against the Backtesting page: all of them (loadInitialWindow()'s initial fitContent(), resetChartZoom(), onChartTimeframeChange()'s setVisibleRange() fallback, onChartTimezoneChange()'s fitContent()) belong to this file's own standalone 'Chart' page, which has had zero route/button/element wiring to reach it since the v3.20.0 Chart->Backtesting rename -- confirmed by tracing every caller, not assumed. No change needed there; see release notes for the full per-site breakdown.
release_notes: No DB migration. Full audit of every fitContent()/setVisibleLogicalRange()/setVisibleRange()/resetTimeScale() call site in app/js/ reachable from the Backtesting page, per the briefing: (1) chart.js:189 loadInitialWindow()'s fitContent() -- unreachable, loadInitialWindow() is only called from loadChart()/onChartSymbolChange()/onChartTimeframeChange(), none of which any page or router entry ever calls (confirmed via grep across every .php/.js file -- zero callers outside chart.js's own definitions). (2) chart.js:210 loadOlderCandles()'s setVisibleLogicalRange() -- already guarded in v3.26.0 (the call to loadOlderCandles() itself is skipped during an active backtest session via the window.btFetchCandlesOverride check). (3) chart.js:306 the dblclick handler's fitContent() -- REACHABLE (the container is #tv-chart, shared with Backtesting) and was NOT guarded; this is the actual bug, fixed this release: now calls btJumpToLatest() during an active session (detected via the same window.btFetchCandlesOverride signal used elsewhere), falls through to the original fitContent() otherwise. (4) chart.js:331 resetChartZoom() -- zero callers anywhere in the codebase, fully dead code. (5) chart.js:391 onChartTimeframeChange()'s setVisibleRange() fallback and (6) chart.js:397 onChartTimezoneChange()'s fitContent() -- both unreachable, same reason as (1). backtest.js/backtest-drawings.js themselves call neither function anywhere (confirmed via grep; backtest.js's own time-axis control is entirely scrollToPosition()-based since v3.26.0). The pre-existing btOnDrawDblClick() (backtest-drawings.js) stopPropagation()-when-a-drawing-is-hit behavior is untouched and still takes priority -- double-clicking an actual drawing still opens its settings popover, never triggers Jump to Latest. Verified: new tools/ui-harness/drive-v3261.mjs (real Playwright mouse events, not JS-console API calls) -- a double-click on empty chart area during an active session leaves bar spacing/scroll position unchanged; a double-click after a manual pan restores the fixed spacing and live edge exactly like the Jump to Latest button; a double-click on an existing drawing still opens its settings popover and does not touch bar spacing. Every pre-existing driver (drive.mjs through drive-v3250.mjs, 11 total, none edited) plus the new drive-v3261.mjs all pass; duplicate-name scan clean; php -l / node --check clean. Two drivers (drive-v3227.mjs, drive-v32210.mjs) intermittently timed out waiting for a backtest_advance network response when run back-to-back with the full ~12-driver suite in this environment -- confirmed via repeated isolated runs (11 standalone runs total, ~18% flake rate reproduced identically on the pre-v3.26.1 baseline with git stash) that this is pre-existing PHP-dev-server-under-load flakiness in this sandboxed environment, unrelated to this change (neither driver touches mouse events, dblclick, or chart.js at all). Not yet verified from this environment, per the user's own note: a double-click and a drag against real BTCUSDT 1H data on the live site -- this environment only has the harness's mock sessions.
